full_judgment:
3. Put briefly, the case of the plaintiffs is that the suit land measuring 0.25 acres of land appertaining to Taluk No. 6299/20 Lal Mohammad belonged to their father Khalilur Rahman Chowdhury. The suit land was marshy and grass growing for grazing cattle. During Cadestral Survey Operation, the suit land was recorded in plot No. 2943 in the name of their father, Khalilur Rahman as son and Jebunessa as daughter. Muktabisur Rahman, thereafter, died leaving behind defendant Nos. 2-4. Jebunessa died leaving behind defendant No.5. The suit land fell in the share of the plaintiffs by amicable arrangement amongst the heirs of Khalilur Rahman and they exercised acts of possession on the suit land by growing paddy. During the Survey Settlement Operation, the defendant No.1 collusively got his name recorded in respect of the said 0.35 acres of land. The plaintiffs, thereupon, filed an objection case and the same was dismissed. Plaintiffs, thereafter, filed an appeal under section 19(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the same was allowed on 31-5-1966 with the order that the land be recorded in the name of the plaintiffs. Against the said decision, the defendant No. 1 preferred a special appeal which was decided against the plaintiffs. On 31st day of May, 1966 the defendant No. 1 having attempted to dispossess the plaintiffs, the latter filed a case against the defendant No. 1 under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the said case was later on converted into a case under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the said 145 proceeding the possession of the suit was found with the plaintiffs. The plaintiff''s criminal case against the defendant No. 1 under section 379 of the Penal Code which was filed for reaping away paddy from the suit land by the defendants was dismissed. The defendant No. 1 being encouraged with the order dated 31-5-1996 passed in the special appeal forcibly dismissed the plaintiff in the middle part of the month of Poush, 1373 BS which compelled the plaintiffs to file the suit. 

 4. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by presenting a written statement traversing all the allegations made in the plaint. In the written statement it is stated that the suit land appertained to Taluk No.702/29 Patta Md Afsar originally belonged to Obaidur Rahman Choudhury in Maliki right and the suit land had been recorded in Cadestral Survey plot No. 2941. It is specifically pleaded that Obaidul Rahman Chowdhury was in khas possession of the plot No.2943 and he settled the said plot No. 2943 to the defendant No. 1 35 years back at a rent of Taka 6 and the defendant has been possessing the same openly and adversely by growing paddy therein. It is also averred that he paid rent to the superior landlords and received Farogs (Rend receipts) from the landlords. It is further stated that the adjacent eastern plot of CS Dag No.2943 is CS Dag No.2828 which appertained to Taluk No.6299 Lal Mohammad and the said plot was purchased by the father of the plaintiffs. It is the further case of the defendant that during the Survey Settlement Operation the entire land of CS Dag No.2943 was recorded as settlement survey Dag No.389 in the name of the defendant No.1. The plea of limitation and adverse possession have been also taken by the defendant No. 1 in the written statement. 

 21. Plaintiff No.1 Nabibur Rahman Chowdhury as PW 1 gave testimony to the effect that they themselves grew paddy on the suit land through servant and thereafter through bargadar and defendant No.1 amalgamated the suit land with his land which lay towards the west. The relevant portion of the evidence is quoted thus "First we ourselves grew paddy therein through servant and later through bargadar. He (defendant No.1) amalgamated the suit land with his land which lies towards the west." On perusal of the cross-examination it does not appear that PW 1 was cross-examined an the statement that the defendant No.1 amalgamated the suit land with his land. PW 2 Samawar Ali testified that he had been sowing the suit land for 23 to 24 years and the suit land was in possession of the plaintiffs. He stated that he bhag cultivated the suit land on behalf of the plaintiffs and the suit land is now in the possession of defendant No.1 for 6/7 years. He further gave testimony that the defendant dispossessed the plaintiffs thereform 6/7 years ago in the month of Poush by planting paddy plant therein and before this dispossession, defendant did not ever possess the suit land. In his cross-examination PW 2 denied the suggestion put forward by the defendant that the plaintiffs are not the owner of the suit land and also that he did not bhag cultivate the suit land. He asserted that defendant No.1 had been possessing the suit land for 7/8 years. This witness correctly stated the area of the land. PW 3 Mahmat Ali gave testimony that he knows the suit land. Further testimony is that the defendant No.1 had been possessing the suit land for 7 to 8 years and he did not know who possessed the suit land before Monohar (Defendant No. 1). The cross-examination of this PW 3 had been declined by the defendant side. Defendant No.1 Monohar Ali as DW 1 gave testimony to the effect that Obaidur Rahman Chowdhury was the owner of the suit land and he took settlement from him 30/31 years ago and he paid him rent and since settlement he had been possessing the suit land. He further testified that the suit land appertained to PS Dag No.381. He further stated that to the north south and west of the suit land is his land and to the east of the suit land is the land of Nabibur Rahman, (plaintiff No.1). He also testified that during his 35 years of possession of the suit land none interrupted him. But there was no testimony by DW 1 to the effect that he did not dispossess the plaintiffs in the middle part of the month of Poush, 1373 BS as alleged by the plaintiffs in paragraph No.8 of the plaint. 

 22. It had already been pointed out that in paragraph No.8 of the plaint it has been stated that the defendant in the middle part of the month of Poush, 1373 BS dispossessed the plaintiffs. The plaintiff No.1 as PW 1 gave evidence that the defendant No.1amalgamated the suit land with his land. PW 2 gave evidence that the suit land was in possession of the plaintiffs and he bhag cultivated the suit land under the plaintiffs and the suit land was under the possession of the defendant No.1 for 6/7 years and the defendant dispossessed the plaintiffs therefrom 6/7 years ago in the month of Poush, 1373 BS. The PW 3, though, stated that the defendant No. 1 had been possessing the suit land for 7/9 years but he did not know who possessed the suit land before the defendant No.1, possessed the suit land 7-8 years back. The claim of possession and the subsequent dispossession of the plaintiffs on the suit land appears to have been established by PW 1 and PW 2 even if the testimony of PW 3 is left out from consideration. It is significant to notice that defendant No. 1, though specifically pleaded of his possession over the suit land for 35 years the alleged possession was not at all corroborated by any evidence whatsoever. Without any corroboration it is difficult to accept the contention of the defendant that he was in possession of the suit land for the last 35 years specially when the foundation of his possession ie the alleged settlement from landlord Obaidur Rahman Chowdhury with respect to Taluk No.702/29 fall to the ground. Law is settled that possession always follows from lawful title. In this case the title of the suit land was not found with the defendant No. 1 and the same was found with the plaintiffs by both the courts below. The defendant No. 1 in the written statement and as well as in the evidence set out the case that he got possession over the suit land for about 35 years back from Obaidur Rahman Chowdhury on the basis of a settlement from him and no case had been set up that the defendant No.1 forcibly entered into possession on the suit land in total denial of the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiffs and the possession was notorious and hostile and as such the question of acquisition of title by adverse possession did not and does not arise. In support of the contention on behalf of the appellant that the plaintiffs having signally failed to prove their possession within 12 years of the institution of the suit, the same stood barred by limitation, reliance has been placed on Ahmed Miaji and others vs Eakub Ali Munshi and others, 12 DLR HC 708, Arabjan Bibi vs Abdul Kadid and others, 19 DLR 743, Syed Main Ahmed vs Kh Mohiuddin, 19 DLR 912; Raman Ali alias Md Rakman Ali and others vs Hasib Ali Chowdhury and others, 24 DLR 146. The judicial views emerging out of the authorities refered to above is that where plaintiff pleads possession and dispossession, the onus is upon him to prove such possession and dispossession and the case will be controlled by Article 142 of the Limitation Act. 

 24. In the result, the appeal is dismissed, however without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court are maintained though not for the reasons stated in the said judgment.
